evidence: Draper Site, Crawford Lake, Saugeen Culture and Iroquoian Peoples are William David Finlayson's archaeological works (7 listed thesis citations). Mons Meg (1948; 1 citation) is credited to W. H. Finlayson in scholarly bibliographies.

The Harlem Renaissance: The One and the Many and Carl Van Vechten and the Harlem Renaissance are Mark Irving Helbling's (5 citation weights). Conceptualizing and Measuring Immigration Policies is coauthored by Marc Helbling (1). The untitled 1972 review remains unresolved; estimated share lies between 5/7 and 6/7.

The Antigonish letter, Campus and the Community, and editorial credit for The Man from Margaree belong to Alexander Fraser Laidlaw (3/6 citation weights). The two Casa di Sallustio studies are Anne Laidlaw's; Cicero and the Stage is catalogued under W. A. Laidlaw. This is an even split, with no LC-person majority.

Major Speeches, Saemaul, Our Nation's Path, Korea Reborn, and The Country, the Revolution, and I / Kukkawa hyongmyonggwa na belong to President Park Chung Hee (6/7 citation weights). JSTOR identifies Protestantism in Late Confucian Korea as Chung-shin Park's article.

Crime Commissions in the United States, Barbarians in Our Midst, Citizens Crime Commissions and The Myth of the Wide-Open Town are Virgil W. Peterson's (4/5 citation weights). V. Spike Peterson's university CV lists The Politics of Identity in International Relations (1993).

The Gates Ajar, The Gates Between and What to Wear? are Elizabeth Stuart Phelps's (3/7 citation weights). The 2009 flashbulb-memory paper and the two neuroscience/race papers identify psychologist Elizabeth A. Phelps as coauthor (4/7).

Chaucer's Pardoner and Gender Theory, Medieval Interpretation, the Aucassin et Nicolette chapter and La(ca)ncelot belong to Robert Stuart Sturges (4/5 citation weights). Malthus and Ricardo's Inductivist Critics is by N. B. de Marchi and R. P. Sturges, a different author.

Social Criticism in Popular Religious Literature and English Devotional Literature are Helen Constance White's (4/5 citation weights), as are the listed metaphysical-poetry works. Captain Fisk Goes to Washington bears Helen McCann White's byline (1/5).

David Haven Blake's university biography identifies Liking Ike and Walt Whitman and the Culture of American Celebrity as his books (2/4 citation weights). The British Library credits Colin Mackenzie: Collector Extraordinary to David M. Blake; the 1981 Times item is journalist David Blake's. This is an even split, with no LC-person majority.

Revolutionizing Motherhood is Marguerite Guzman Bouvard's (3/4 citation weights). The publisher identifies Transparency in the Financial System: Rollover Risk and Crises as an article by Matthieu Bouvard, Pierre Chaigneau and Adolfo de Motta (1/4).
